svg.aria-label: Figure 1.5: The Sumerian Canal, Tax, Ration, and Trade Loop
svg.text: The Sumerian Canal, Tax, Ration, and Trade Loop
How southern Mesopotamia turned river water and barley surplus into cities, wool exports, and imported timber and metal

g.text: Natural silt levees sit above plain
Turn local wool into export cloth
Sumer lacked stone, ore, & tall timber
Trade cloth for wood, ore & stone

text.tspan: Poor drainage and 45°C+ summer evaporation drew mineral salts into southern topsoil, cutting salt-sensitive wheat

svg.text: from ~16% to under 2% of grain harvests and helping shift political power northward toward Babylon. (Ration standards shown span c. 3200–2000 BCE.)
